audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in this matchup, and that was accurate — Wither was named repeatedly with no number and no "wait for X, then Y" instruction.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s on a 700 range. That is a genuinely long gap for a champion whose entire counterplay to Zac is one button, and it is the difference between a slingshot that kills and a slingshot that gets walked out of. Spirit Fire is a flat 12s at every rank and shreds armour, so it is the second clock worth counting.
audit.corrected: Wither 15s at rank 1 — commit inside that window, never into it. Spirit Fire flat 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text claims Wither "neuters W Unstable Matter windups".
audit.why: Unstable Matter is a flat 5s point-blank burst with no wind-up at all, and Wither decelerates Move Speed and Attack Speed — neither of which touches an instant ability cast. The real cost of Wither is that it ends the chase after your slingshot lands.
audit.corrected: Wither kills the chase, not the cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike being an auto-attack reset was never mentioned, and neither was its 255 range.
audit.why: A 255-range Q forces Nasus to stand inside Zac's Q (800) and W (350) to farm — that is why the early lane is free. The auto reset also means the burst tell is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast, which is what _missing-interactions.json flags as autoreset-burst-tell for this pairing.
audit.corrected: Nasus has to walk to 255 range to stack; his Q is an auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Late-game advice named Spirit Visage and Thornmail as Nasus's items but never told the Zac player to buy Grievous Wounds, and never warned that Heartsteel stacking is partly self-defeating here.
audit.why: Nasus's sustain is Soul Eater lifesteal, so anti-heal is the counter. Separately, Fury of the Sands deals a percentage of max health — _missing-interactions.json flags this as resistances-invalidated. A Zac who answers Nasus by stacking raw HP is feeding the one damage source that scales off it.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is mandatory; Fury of the Sands burns %max HP, so HP alone is the wrong answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described only as "his Wither counters your dives".
audit.why: Fury of the Sands also grants bonus Health, bonus Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resist, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown and a %max-health damage aura, for 120s at rank 1. Wither is the smaller half of what changes at 6.
audit.corrected: At 6 the ult is the spike, not the slow.

audit.why: Content win[] reads Zac, Zac, Zac, Zac, Skill, Nasus, Nasus against a 54.04% Zac win rate over 161 games. Early Zac dominance decaying into Nasus scaling is exactly right and is consistent with the record.

edits.before: Once you have E Elastic Slingshot up, you own this lane: charge from brush and Q Stretching Strikes double-hit a Nasus who has to walk into minions to last-hit, denying his Siphoning Strike stacks.
edits.after: Once E Elastic Slingshot is up you own this lane: charge from brush and Q-double-hit a Nasus stuck at 255 range to last-hit; his Q is an auto reset, so the wind-up is your tell, not the cast.

edits.before: After his first item Nasus starts hitting a Wither-and-Q combo that shuts down your kiting; Wither on you neuters W Unstable Matter windups and your slingshot chase.
edits.after: After his first item Nasus hits a Wither-and-Q combo that ends your chase; Wither is 15s at rank 1, so slingshot in the window after he spends it, never into it.

edits.before: Level 6 is even — his Wither counters your dives just as your R comes online.
edits.after: Level 6 is even — Fury of the Sands burns %HP as Wither ends your chase.

edits.before: Through level 5 you remain the bully; keep denying stacks and pressuring his wave. Level 6 evens out — his Wither now cancels your slingshot chases and W windups, and once he buys his first item the lane flips.
edits.after: Through level 5 you remain the bully; keep denying stacks and pressuring his wave. Level 6 evens out — Wither is 15s at rank 1 and ends your chase, and Fury of the Sands burns %max HP, so wait it out before you commit.

edits.before: With stacks and Spirit Visage/Thornmail online Nasus outheals and outdamages your kit in any extended fight, so stop dueling him — build tanky, use R to peel your carries and win via cross-map pressure you banked early.
edits.after: With stacks and lifesteal online Nasus outheals your kit in any extended fight, so Grievous Wounds is not optional — and Fury of the Sands burns %max HP, so raw Heartsteel stacking feeds him. Peel with R and cash the early lead.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Trade around it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nasus Wither (W, 15s at rank 1): matchup-defining — his only stick tool; commit inside that window, never into it. - Spirit Fire (flat 12s): shreds your armour. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands adds HP, range and a %max-HP burn at 6 — reassess every all-in, and never open one inside an active Wither.

notes: Both packet suspectNames for this matchup are FALSE POSITIVES. 'Let's Bounce' in spikes[1] is already written "Let's Bounce!" on disk — the detector strips the exclamation mark. 'Spirit Visage' in `late` was matched against Nasus's E 'Spirit Fire' at edit distance 4, but Spirit Visage is a real item and the sentence was about Nasus's build, not his abilities. I rewrote that sentence anyway, for the anti-heal and %max-HP reasons above, not because the name was wrong.
